“allow me in the setup to rearrange the business units table so they appear in the navigation as per this order and let’s clean this table making a three dots option to actions like the registry file”

Settled

  • The mark leaves the table and lives only in the unit’s settings.
  • The group’s Performance page keeps its own Arrange for these cards.
  • Companies is in scope — the three dots, and no dragging.

What the numbers say

Four controls stacked in one cell — the pen, Retire, Clear progress, Clear plan — on every row. The People register, which already has the three dots, runs at 39px.

What it costs

  • You lose the at-a-glance answer to “which units have no mark”. Today the marks table shows all ten side by side. It becomes one dialog a unit. Every one of the ten currently has a mark, so nothing is outstanding — but that is the trade, and it is stated rather than discovered.
  • Uploading a mark becomes two presses (three dots → Edit details) where today it is one, on a section you had to scroll to reach.
  • Editing moves off the row. Correcting ten code prefixes becomes ten dialogs rather than ten pens in place. The register made this trade and it was the right one, but it is a real change to how a bulk tidy-up feels.

What I build on your go-ahead

  • Business units — the table above, the dialog with the mark in it, the menu, and Arrange. The Unit marks section is deleted, not hidden.
  • Functions — Arrange, and “Edit this row” becoming “Edit details” on the same dialog.
  • Companies — the three dots, carrying the refusal.
  • A check that presses every control and reads the stored order back, run against today’s build first so it is proved able to fail before its green is believed.
  • No migration, no schema change, no server change. The order is already a stored column and the server already calls a change to it the office’s.
